outline.description: This chapter establishes the legal foundation of the case by explaining the roles of the Office of Special Counsel (OSC) and the various statutes governing FOIA enforcement and personnel practices. It also outlines the specific facts regarding the Department of Justice's email search policy and the litigation timeline.
subtopics: The Role of the Office of Special Counsel (OSC)
The Department of Justice's Email Search Policy
Procedural History: From FOIA Litigation to the OSC Complaint

outline.chapter_title: Constitutional Requirements for Article III Standing
outline.description: This chapter details the constitutional requirements for a plaintiff to bring a case to federal court. It focuses on the 'case-or-controversy' requirement and the specific elements necessary to establish standing.
subtopics: The Case-or-Controversy Requirement under Article III
The Three-Part Test: Injury-in-Fact, Causation, and Redressability
Relaxed Standing Standards for Procedural Injuries

outline.chapter_title: Analysis of the FOIA Records Standing Theory
outline.description: This chapter examines the court's analysis of the first standing theory presented by the plaintiff: that the OSC's failure to investigate caused the denial of FOIA records. It explores why the court found this theory to be legally insufficient.
subtopics: The Plaintiff's Claim of Informational Injury
Speculation Regarding Independent Actors (MSPB and DOJ)
The Limits of Redressability and Judicial Binding Power

outline.chapter_title: Analysis of the Informational Standing Theory
outline.description: This chapter explores the second standing theory: that the plaintiff is entitled to the 'fruits' of the OSC investigation itself. It explains the distinction between mandatory duties and discretionary procedures in administrative law.
subtopics: OSC's Discretionary Authority over Procedural Requirements
Final Disposition and Vacatur of the District Court Judgment
